## TL;DR

This source tree contains the macOS Hub QA record and XCTest registry isolation fixes. The current acceptance evidence covers build, launch, first-run rendering, local server discovery and connection, and the sign-in page. Authenticated Projects and Tasks remain unverified because human follow-up #1174 has no results. This report is for the checked worktree at `8daea03ae447b2959c684762c514d1838a1a23f1`.

## Work and rationale

The macOS QA work built the Hub with Xcode using signing disabled and its own DerivedData directory, then launched it through LaunchServices with an isolated support directory. It verified the first-run empty state, discovery and health checking of a local RepoOS server, adding and persisting that server, and rendering the connected sign-in page. The QA record documents the exercised paths, known limitations, and app-window-only captures.

The run found that an XCTest app host could write to the developer's ordinary Hub registry when no support-directory override was configured. The app now uses a unique temporary support directory for XCTest unless an explicit override is set, removes the scratch directory on termination, logs cleanup errors, and tests cleanup and error propagation. The QA record also discloses the initial registry write and unknown prior selection rather than claiming it was restored.

## Approaches tried

Built and launched with isolated storage and inspected the native Hub window and accessibility tree while exercising first-run and add-server flows. A healthy local connection showed the sign-in page. A direct executable launch did not produce a content window during the brief observation; this is recorded as unexplained rather than a confirmed crash. Automated email-code interaction did not reach authenticated screens. Stored RepoOS report artifacts were not edited manually.

## Challenges and blockers

A human must complete the authorized email-code sign-in, inspect Projects and Tasks, and report both results in #1174. That task remains assigned to a human with no results, so the authenticated acceptance criterion is still open. The full `repoos check` is being run against this worktree before handoff; RepoOS will generate the immutable report metadata and tree summary after the check passes.

## Key learnings

A rendered sign-in page proves connection and web rendering, not authenticated functionality. The Projects and Tasks acceptance needs direct observations recorded by the human follow-up. XCTest app-host processes need isolated support storage to protect a developer's registry, and cleanup failures should be visible. RepoOS consumes a draft into a per-round report at handoff, so a new draft is required after each missing-draft failure.
